A1.justification: Both readable, 10-page PDFs describe the same TEAR work and support reliable comparison of the supplied content. However, neither contains the appendices referenced in Sections 4.1–4.2 for baseline implementation details and safe-seed experiments, so those materials cannot be compared.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original TEAR evaluations, including baseline comparisons, commercial-model attacks, sensitivity analyses, and transferability results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised generation-setting sensitivity results in Figure 6(c–d).

M1.justification: The generator training, temporal rewards, PPO objective, and refinement procedure remain unchanged. Corrections to the rewritten-prompt symbol and refine-model notation do not alter the method.

E1.justification: The supplied content retains the same 390 seed prompts, six harmful categories, five target T2V systems, seed-free evaluations, and transfer scenarios. Figure 6 changes generation configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Naive, T2VSafetyBench, UVD, FLIRT, and ART; Table 2 retains FLIRT and ART. Table 1's UVG label becomes UVD, matching the method already identified in v1 Section 4.1, without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Figure 6(c–d) replaces the 'Video Length' settings 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 with 'Number of Frames' settings 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, retaining the CFG-scale grid. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Other stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The generation-length/CFG sensitivity analysis in Figure 6(c–d) is revised with different settings and results. Refinement-round analysis, prompt diversity, transferability analysis, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 6(c–d) replaces the ASR and NSFW-pass matrices: their ranges change from 76.67–83.85% and 96.15–97.69% to 74.87–85.90% and 95.13–97.44%, respectively. These concern revised settings, not a demonstrated same-setting gain. Figure 4's prose corrects '83%–0.95%' to '83%–95%'; Tables 1–3 remain numerically identical.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, MDP description, and Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. Local symbol corrections introduce no new definitions, assumptions, proofs, or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the temporal-vulnerability contribution, claimed superiority over prior methods, over-80% versus approximately 57% performance claim, and cross-model transferability claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 removes the explicit interpretation that further refinement gains become harder as prompts become more optimized, while retaining the observation of slowing improvement. Other mechanism explanations and applicability claims remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces direct Qwen3-VL repository and RoBERTa/Llama-Guard checkpoint references with paper citations, removing specific resource-access pointers. The stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged, and no additional baseline implementation appendix is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Cao et al.'s rule-based preference-modeling work and explicitly credits the already-cited T2VSafetyBench as the first T2V safety benchmark. Model-resource citations are updated, while TEAR's overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammatical, spelling, notation, and baseline-label corrections, shortens several discussion passages, updates affiliations and corresponding-author markers, and adds acknowledgments. The section sequence and overall narrative remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6(c–d) receives revised axis labels, ticks, titles, and captions alongside its changed heatmaps. Table 3 moves above the Section 4.3 heading, and text and figure placement shift modestly. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Corrected notation, baseline naming, the Figure 4 percentage typo, and clearer frame-count labels improve clarity. Conversely, removing exact model-access pointers reduces reproducibility information. Figure 6's revised settings and results do not establish an evidential improvement, while the main comparisons remain unchanged. These limited benefits and losses leave the net overall quality direction uncertain.
